Repo tiny: 5 files, `src/`, no package.json, no tests, no deps. CommonJS, Node built-ins only (`node:http`, `node:crypto`).

## Layers

Request flow top to bottom:

```
server.js  -> auth.js       (gate: 401 or user)
   |
routes.js  -> cache.js      (reads: read-through LRU)
   |       -> store.js      (writes: direct)
```

**`server.js`** — thin HTTP front. Every request hits `verifyToken` first. No token = `401`, done. Else pass `(req, res, user)` to `route`. Listens on `PORT` or 8080 when run direct; exports `createServer` so tests/embedders can drive it.

**`auth.js`** — HMAC bearer tokens, format `<userId>.<hexsig>`, sig = HMAC-SHA256 of userId under `AUTH_SECRET` (falls back `'dev-secret'`). `verifyToken` returns `{id: userId}` or null. Compare via `timingSafeEqual`, length-checked first so it not throw.

**`routes.js`** — flat dispatch table keyed `"METHOD /path"`. 3 routes: `GET /users`, `GET /orders`, `POST /orders`. Miss = 404. Handler result wrapped in `Promise.resolve`, so sync and async handlers both work; resolve = 200 JSON, reject = 500 with `err.message`. `parseQuery` turns search params into plain object.

**`cache.js`** — 256-entry LRU, module-level `Map`. Insertion order = recency; hit does delete+set to bump, overflow evicts `keys().next().value` (oldest). No TTL by design.

**`store.js`** — in-memory `Map` standing in for DB. Per-record 15-min TTL, checked lazily on `get` (expired record deleted on read, no sweeper). `putOrder` reads the list, pushes, rewrites whole array — so TTL resets on each write.

## Three things stand out before you build on it

1. **Cache invalidation missing.** `routes.js:5` comment says writes "invalidate the affected keys" — no code does that. `POST /orders` writes to store but never touches `lru`. Once `orders:<id>` cached, new orders invisible until LRU evicts it. Cache has no TTL either, so stale can be permanent.

2. **Cache outlives store TTL.** Store expires records at 15 min; cache holds forever. Read-through means cache absorbs the first read and never re-asks — so `getUser` returns a user the store already dropped.

3. **`POST /orders` never reads request body.** `q` comes from `parseQuery` = URL search params only. `q.body` is `undefined` unless caller sends `?body=...`. Request stream never consumed. So orders array fills with `undefined`.

Also: `verifyToken` splits on `.` and takes first two parts — a userId containing `.` mis-parses. Low risk if IDs numeric.

Want me fix 1–3?
